overview.intro:
Chapter 83 covers miscellaneous articles of base metal: padlocks, locks and keys (8301), hinges, castors, door, window and furniture fittings, drawer slides and brackets (8302), safes (8303), desk equipment (8304), binder fittings, paper clips and staples (8305), bells, ornaments, picture frames and mirrors (8306), flexible tubing (8307), clasps, buckles, eyelets and rivets (8308), caps, crown corks and can ends (8309), sign plates (8310) and welding electrodes and solder (8311). **16 of the 89 lines are Free**; the rest pay from 2% to 7.5% (hooks and eyes 1.1¢/kg + 2.9%).

Two regimes split the chapter. **31 lines are Section 232 aluminum or steel derivatives** (U.S. note 16(c)(vi)–(vii)): hinges, castors, door closers and the door, furniture and vehicle fittings of iron, steel, aluminum or zinc, drawer slides, brackets, binder fittings, staples in strips, frames and mirrors, flexible tubing without fittings, and aluminum or steel caps and can ends. Since April 6, 2026 they pay **+25% of the full customs value** (9903.82.09) from every country, on top of any FTA or USMCA rate, and no 2026 Section 301 or Brazil duty. Lower rates: **10%** when at least 85% of the metal was melted or smelted in the United States, **15%** for UK goods with 95% UK metal, and **no Section 232 duty** when aluminum, steel and copper together are under 15% of the article's weight (9903.82.03).

The other **58 lines** (locks and keys, brass hardware, safes, desk equipment, bells and ornaments, tubing with fittings, buckles and rivets, crown corks, sign plates, welding consumables) pay the base rate plus the **2026 Section 301** duty of 10% or 12.5% for 60 economies (EU, Japan, Korea and Taiwan: 10% or 12.5% in place of a lower base rate); USMCA goods of Canada and Mexico are exempt. Vehicle locks, hinges and fittings (8301.20, 8302.10.30, 8302.30) pay the **auto-parts duty** instead when used in cars or trucks.

China pays **25% (List 3) or 7.5% (List 4A)** more on 81 lines; Canada pays **+50% under Section 338** on 18 lines even with a USMCA claim. Chinese aluminum-extrusion hardware, paper clips and collated staples also carry **antidumping and countervailing duties**, which are company-specific and not in this table (see Tariff updates).

productGroups.label: Padlocks, locks & keys
productGroups.blurb: Padlocks, door locks and locksets, furniture, luggage and motor-vehicle locks, clasps with locks, lock parts and keys: 19 lines, 2.3% to 6.1%. None is on the Section 232 metals lists, so most countries pay the base rate plus the 2026 Section 301 duty (10% or 12.5%; USMCA goods exempt). Vehicle locks (8301.20) pay the auto-parts duty instead when they are car or truck parts. China: List 4A (7.5%) on most lines; Canadian lock parts pay +50% Section 338.

productGroups.label: Hinges, castors & mountings and fittings
productGroups.blurb: Hinges, castors, door closers, door, window and curtain hardware, drawer slides and other furniture fittings, motor-vehicle fittings, saddlery hardware, brackets and hat racks: 36 lines, Free to 7.5%. The 22 lines of iron, steel, aluminum or zinc (plus castors, brackets and door closers) are Section 232 aluminum or steel derivatives: +25% of the full value. Fittings of other base metal such as brass (8302.10.90, 8302.41.90, 8302.42.60, 8302.49.80) are outside Section 232. Chinese aluminum-extrusion fittings are under AD/CVD orders.

productGroups.label: Safes & strong-boxes
productGroups.blurb: Armored or reinforced safes, gun safes, strong-boxes, strong-room doors and safe-deposit lockers, cash and deed boxes: 1 line, 3.8%. Not on the Section 232 lists: most countries pay the 2026 Section 301 duty, China 25% (List 3) + 12.5%, and Canadian safes +50% Section 338 even under USMCA.

productGroups.label: Desk-top filing cabinets & desk equipment
productGroups.blurb: Desk-top filing or card-index cabinets, paper trays, paper rests, pen trays, office-stamp stands and similar desk equipment of base metal (office furniture is 9403): 1 line, 3.9%. Outside Section 232; Chinese goods are on the suspended List 4B, so they pay only the 12.5% 2026 Section 301 duty.

productGroups.label: Binder fittings, paper clips & staples
productGroups.blurb: Ring-binder mechanisms and other looseleaf fittings, staples in strips (collated staples), paper clips, letter clips, indexing tags and similar office articles: 6 lines, Free to 5.7%. Staples in strips (8305.20) and other binder fittings (8305.10.00.50) are Section 232 derivatives (+25%). Chinese paper clips and collated staples are under antidumping orders (staples also countervailing).

productGroups.label: Bells, ornaments, frames & mirrors
productGroups.blurb: Non-electric bells, gongs and chimes, statuettes and other ornaments (plated with precious metal or not), and photograph or picture frames and mirrors of base metal: 4 lines, Free to 5.8%. Frames and mirrors (8306.30) are an aluminum derivative under Section 232 (+25%); other ornaments (8306.29) from Canada pay +50% Section 338.

productGroups.label: Flexible metal tubing
productGroups.blurb: Flexible tubing of iron or steel (including jacketed corrugated stainless gas tubing) or of other base metal, with or without fittings: 5 lines, all 3.8%. Tubing without fittings (8307.10.60, 8307.90.60) is a Section 232 derivative (+25%); tubing with fittings is not, but from Canada it pays +50% Section 338.

productGroups.label: Clasps, buckles, hooks, eyelets & rivets
productGroups.blurb: Hooks, eyes and eyelets, tubular and bifurcated rivets, buckles and buckle clasps, clasps and frames with clasps, beads and spangles of base metal (for clothing, footwear, bags and the like): 6 lines, Free to 3.9% (hooks, eyes and eyelets 1.1¢/kg + 2.9%). Not on the Section 232 lists; all 6 lines pay Canada's 50% Section 338 duty and China's 25% List 3.

productGroups.label: Stoppers, caps, lids & closures
productGroups.blurb: Crown corks, screw caps, beverage-can ends, pouring stoppers, bungs, capsules, seals and other packing accessories of base metal: 5 lines, Free or 2.6%. Aluminum can ends and other aluminum closures (8309.90.00.20, .25) and steel closures (.80) are Section 232 derivatives (+25%); crown corks are not, but from Canada they pay +50% Section 338.

productGroups.label: Sign plates, name plates & numbers
productGroups.blurb: Sign plates, name plates, address plates and similar plates, numbers, letters and other symbols of base metal (illuminated signs are 9405): 1 line, Free. Not on Section 232. It is on CBP's informational-materials list, so the 2026 Section 301 and Brazil duties do not apply to plates that qualify; China's 25% List 3 and Canada's 50% Section 338 still do.

productGroups.label: Welding electrodes, wire & solder
productGroups.blurb: Coated electrodes and cored wire for electric arc welding, lead-tin solders and other coated rods and cored wire for soldering, brazing or flame welding, and metal-spraying wire: 5 lines, all Free. Not on the Section 232 lists (solid welding wire is classified with its metal in Chapters 72–76). The 2026 Section 301 duty applies; Canada +50% Section 338 on four lines; China 25% List 3.

workedExamples.title: $50,000 of steel door hinges from Vietnam
workedExamples.body: Door hinges of steel carry a **3.5%** base rate. They are on the Section 232 derivative lists (note 16(c)(vi) and (vii)), so they pay **+25% of their full value** (9903.82.09): **28.5%**, or $14,250. The 12.5% 2026 Section 301 duty on Vietnam does not apply to Section 232 goods (note 52(f)(1)). If at least 85% of the steel was melted and poured in the United States, the 232 part drops to **10%** (9903.82.06): 13.5%.

workedExamples.title: Steel drawer slides from China
workedExamples.body: Base rate **3.9%**, plus **+7.5%** Section 301 (List 4A, 9903.88.15) and **+25%** Section 232 (9903.82.09): **36.4%**. China's 12.5% 2026 Section 301 duty is replaced by Section 232; the List 4A duty is not. Aluminum drawer slides from China can also fall under the aluminum extrusions AD/CVD orders: check the producer's rate.

workedExamples.title: Door locksets from Mexico, with and without USMCA
workedExamples.body: Door locks are not on the Section 232 lists. Without a USMCA claim: **5.7%** base + **10%** Section 301 (9903.05.55) = **15.7%**. With a USMCA certification of origin the base rate is Free and the Section 301 duty does not apply (9903.05.94): **Free**.

workedExamples.title: Welding electrodes from Canada
workedExamples.body: Free at base, but on the Section 338 list since September 15, 2026 (9903.03.14, U.S. note 51(b)(3)): **+50%** even under USMCA. Without a USMCA claim the 10% Section 301 duty (9903.05.29) is added too: **60%**; with USMCA, **50%**.

workedExamples.title: A car door lock from Japan
workedExamples.body: Base rate 5.7%. Used as a part of a car or light truck, it pays Japan's auto-parts rate of **15% in place of the base rate** (9903.94.43) and no Section 301 duty. As a truck or bus part it pays 5.7% + 25% (9903.74.08) = **30.7%**. Otherwise, the Japan Section 301 rate of **12.5% in place of the base rate** (9903.05.49) applies.

tariffUpdates.intro:
This page compares the **2025 Basic Edition** (in force January 1, 2025) with the current **2026 Revision 21** (in force October 9, 2026) and lists every extra duty that reaches Chapter 83 today. No base rate changed; ten statistical lines are new splits of existing ones (copper lock parts and keys, corrugated stainless gas tubing, and aluminum, steel and other caps and can ends).

The extra duties changed completely. In January 2025 Chapter 83 paid only its base rates, plus Section 301 on Chinese goods. On **March 12, 2025** 24 hardware lines (hinges, castors, fittings, brackets, door closers, binder fittings, frames) became Section 232 **aluminum derivatives**, charged on their aluminum content (25%, then 50% from June 4, 2025). On **August 18, 2025** Commerce's inclusions process added steel hinges, door and furniture fittings, staples in strips, flexible steel tubing and aluminum caps. Proclamation 11021 rebuilt the program on **April 6, 2026**: **25% of the full value** for all 31 Chapter 83 derivative lines, with a 15% metal-weight threshold and lower rates for U.S.-melted and UK metal.

The IEEPA tariffs ended on **February 24, 2026** and the Section 122 surcharge on **July 23, 2026**. Since **July 24, 2026** the 2026 Section 301 duties (10% or 12.5%) apply to the 58 lines outside Section 232, Brazil has paid 25% more on them since July 22, and since **August 22 / September 15, 2026** 18 lines from Canada pay a 50% Section 338 duty. Antidumping and countervailing duty orders on Chinese aluminum extrusions, paper clips and collated staples reach parts of the chapter; they are company-specific and **not included in the tariff calculator**.
tariffUpdates.scope: Chapter 99 measures that reach Chapter 83 from any country: Section 232 aluminum and steel derivatives (notes 16 and 19), the Section 232 automobile and medium/heavy-duty vehicle parts duties on vehicle locks, hinges and fittings (notes 33 and 38), China Section 301 (note 20), the 2026 Section 301 actions on 60 economies and Brazil (notes 50, 52), Canada Section 338 (note 51), Russia's column 2 rates and 35% in lieu of column 2 (note 30), the scheduled Nicaragua Section 301 duty (note 29), and the ended IEEPA and Section 122 duties. The antidumping and countervailing duty orders on Chapter 83 products are summarized for reference; the calculator does not model them. For the rate each supplier pays, see Rates by country.

inEffect.country: All countries (Canada, Mexico, EU, Japan, Korea and Brazil included)
inEffect.measure: Section 232 derivative aluminum and steel articles, on the full customs value
inEffect.before: None in January 2025; from March 12, 2025 +25% (from June 4, 2025 +50%) on the aluminum or steel content of the listed lines
inEffect.exemption: Covers 31 lines on U.S. note 16(c)(vi) (aluminum derivatives) and (vii) (steel derivatives): hinges of iron, steel, aluminum or zinc (8302.10.30, 8302.10.60), castors (8302.20), motor-vehicle fittings (8302.30.30), door closers and their parts (8302.41.30, 8302.60), building, furniture and other fittings of iron, steel, aluminum or zinc (8302.41.60, 8302.42.30 incl. drawer slides, 8302.49.60), brackets and hat racks (8302.50), binder fittings other than ring-binder mechanisms (8305.10.00.50), staples in strips (8305.20), frames and mirrors (8306.30), flexible tubing without fittings (8307.10.60, 8307.90.60) and aluminum or steel caps, lids and can ends (8309.90.00.20, .25, .80). No country exemptions; note 16(b) collects it on top of any FTA or USMCA rate. Lower rates: ≥85% of the metal melted/smelted in the United States 10% (9903.82.06); UK goods with ≥95% UK metal 15% (9903.82.05). No duty when aluminum, steel and copper together are under 15% of the article's weight (9903.82.03; Chapter 83 is outside Chapters 72–76) or when it contains none (9903.82.01). Civil aircraft articles of the EU, Japan, Korea and the UK on five of these subheadings (8302.10.60, 8302.20, 8302.42.30, 8302.49.60, 8302.60.30) are exempt (9903.02.76, 9903.96.02, 9903.02.81, 9903.96.01). Vehicle hinges and fittings (8302.10.30, 8302.30.30) pay the auto or truck parts duty instead when used as such. Goods under 9903.82.09 do not pay the 2026 Section 301 or Brazil duties (notes 52(f)(1), 50(a)(vi)(1)); China's Section 301 lists still apply.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Hinges, castors, drawer slides, door closers, brackets, frames, collated staples and can ends pay a quarter of their value in duty from every country: $100,000 of hinges owes $25,000 plus the base rate.

inEffect.country: 60 Section 301 economies (Mexico, Canada, EU, Japan, Korea, Taiwan, Vietnam, India, Thailand, UK, Russia and others)
inEffect.before: None (the IEEPA reciprocal duties until February 24, 2026, then the Section 122 surcharge until July 23, 2026)
inEffect.now: +10% or +12.5% (EU, Japan, Korea, Taiwan: 10% or 12.5% in place of the base rate) on the 58 lines outside Section 232
inEffect.exemption: Does not apply to Section 232 goods (note 52(f)(1), 9903.05.90) or to locks, hinges and fittings that pay the auto or truck parts duty (52(f)(3), (6)). USMCA-qualifying goods of Canada and Mexico are exempt (9903.05.93, 9903.05.94). Sign plates of 8310 that are informational materials are exempt (9903.05.92). Civil aircraft articles on note 52(d)'s list (9903.05.88) are exempt. No Chapter 83 line is on the note 52(b) general exemption list or on the note 52(j) country exception lists.
inEffect.whatItMeans: $100,000 of padlocks, safes, buckles or welding rods from India pays $10,000 on top of the base rate; from Thailand or Vietnam $12,500; the same goods from Mexico with a USMCA certificate pay nothing extra.

inEffect.measure: Section 301: Lists 3 and 4A (2018–2019 actions) and the 2026 action
inEffect.now: +25% or +7.5%, plus 12.5% on the lines outside Section 232 (25% Section 232 on the others)
inEffect.exemption: List 3 (9903.88.03, 25%) covers 57 lines: vehicle locks, most hinges, castors and fittings, safes, frames and mirrors, flexible tubing, buckles and rivets, caps, sign plates and welding consumables. List 4A (9903.88.15, 7.5%) covers 24: most padlocks and locks, lock parts and keys, vehicle hinges, furniture fittings including drawer slides, binder fittings, staples in strips, other office articles (8305.90.60) and plated ornaments. 8 lines are on the suspended List 4B and pay no 2018–2019 duty: large padlocks (8301.10.50, 8301.10.90), luggage locks, desk equipment (8304), paper clips (8305.90.30), bells and other ornaments (8306.10, 8306.29). No product exclusion for Chapter 83 is in effect (notes 20(vvv)–(www)). The 12.5% 2026 duty (9903.05.31) stacks with the lists on the 58 lines outside Section 232. The IEEPA duties on China ended February 24, 2026; USTR confirmed on October 7, 2026 that the 2018–2019 actions continue.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Chinese hinges and door fittings pay about 54% (25% + 25% + base); drawer slides 36.4%; most Chinese padlocks and locks 22–26%; safes 41.3%; welding electrodes 37.5%.

inEffect.now: +25% + 12.5% on the 58 lines outside Section 232; 25% Section 232 on the others
inEffect.exemption: The Brazil duty does not apply to Section 232 goods (note 50(a)(vi)(1), 9903.05.07), informational materials (9903.05.09, which includes 8310 plates that qualify) or civil aircraft articles (9903.05.05).
inEffect.whatItMeans: Brazilian locks, safes or welding electrodes pay the base rate plus 37.5%; Brazilian hinges and fittings pay 25% Section 232 only.

inEffect.now: +50% on 18 lines, with or without a USMCA claim
inEffect.exemption: Since August 22, 2026: lock parts (8301.60), safes (8303) and other base-metal ornaments (8306.29). Since September 15, 2026 (Proclamation 11065, Annex II): flexible tubing with fittings (8307.10.30, 8307.90.30), all of 8308 (hooks, eyelets, rivets, buckles, beads, clasps), crown corks (8309.10), sign plates (8310) and welding electrodes, cored wire and solders (8311.10, 8311.20, 8311.30). None of these is a Section 232 line. Charged even when USMCA is claimed (note 51(a)); without a USMCA claim the 10% Section 301 duty (9903.05.29) is added. Canadian civil aircraft articles are exempt (9903.03.16).
inEffect.whatItMeans: Canadian safes, buckles, crown corks, sign plates and welding electrodes pay 50% of their value (60% plus base without a USMCA claim).

inEffect.country: All countries (EU, Japan, Korea, Taiwan and UK at deal rates)
inEffect.measure: Section 232 automobile and medium/heavy-duty vehicle parts (locks, hinges, fittings)
inEffect.now: +25% (EU, Japan, Korea, Taiwan: 15% in place of the base rate; UK 10%) when used as vehicle parts
inEffect.exemption: Reaches 6 lines of note 33(g): locks for motor vehicles (8301.20), hinges designed for motor vehicles (8302.10.30) and motor-vehicle mountings and fittings (8302.30), when they are parts of passenger vehicles or light trucks (note 33) or of medium and heavy-duty trucks and buses (note 38). Then the metals duty and the 2026 Section 301 duty do not apply. USMCA-qualifying parts of Canada and Mexico are exempt (9903.94.06, 9903.74.10). Not used as vehicle parts, the lines pay Section 232 metals (8302.10.30, 8302.30.30) or the 2026 Section 301 duty (8301.20, 8302.30.60).
inEffect.whatItMeans: A German car lock pays 15% in total; the same lock for a heavy truck pays 5.7% + 25%; a Mexican USMCA-qualifying lock pays nothing.

inEffect.measure: Column 2 rates, 35% in lieu of column 2, Section 232 aluminum (200%) and the 2026 Section 301 duty
inEffect.before: Column 2 rates; 35% in their place on 3 lines; 200% on 24 aluminum-derivative lines from March 12, 2025
inEffect.now: Column 2 rate + 12.5%; +200% on 27 aluminum-derivative lines (up to 257.5%); +25% on the steel-only derivatives
inEffect.exemption: Russia has paid column 2 rates since April 9, 2022. Note 30(b) puts 8302.30.30 and 8305.20 at 35% in place of column 2 (9903.90.08, since July 27, 2022). The 27 aluminum-derivative lines pay 200% (9903.85.68, U.S. note 19(m)), which also applies to such articles from any country when the primary aluminum was smelted, or the article cast, in Russia. Steel derivatives pay 25% (9903.82.16). The 12.5% 2026 Section 301 duty (9903.05.66) is lifted only for the 9903.82 lines.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Russian aluminum or zinc hinges and door fittings pay 45% (column 2) + 200% + 12.5% = 257.5% of their value.

changes.title: No Chapter 83 base-rate changes
changes.detail: 79 of 89 Chapter 83 lines carry the same rates in 2026 Revision 21 as in the 2025 Basic Edition. Ten statistical lines are new splits at unchanged rates: lock parts and keys of copper or copper alloys (8301.60.00.10, 8301.70.00.10; rest .60), jacketed corrugated stainless steel "Fuel Gas" tubing (8307.10.60.10; rest .60), and caps and lids split into aluminum beverage-can ends (8309.90.00.20), other aluminum (.25), steel (.80) and other (.85).

changes.title: Section 338 duty extended to 14 more Canadian Chapter 83 lines
changes.detail: Proclamation 11065 added flexible tubing with fittings (8307.10.30, 8307.90.30), hooks, eyelets, rivets, buckles, beads and clasps (all of 8308), crown corks (8309.10), sign plates (8310) and welding electrodes, cored wire and solders (8311.10, 8311.20, 8311.30) to the 50% list (9903.03.14), and made the duty apply in addition to Section 232. Charged even when USMCA is claimed.

changes.title: Section 338 duty on certain Canadian goods begins
changes.detail: Proclamation 11048 imposed a 50% duty on the products of Canada in the note 51(b) lists from August 22, 2026 (after Proclamation 11056's three-day suspension). In Chapter 83 it reached lock parts (8301.60), safes (8303) and other base-metal ornaments (8306.29), with or without a USMCA claim.

changes.title: 2026 Section 301 tariffs on 60 economies: the non-232 lines pay
changes.detail: The 10% or 12.5% duties on goods of 60 economies (9903.05.20–9903.05.84) took effect. They do not apply to Section 232 goods (note 52(f)(1)) or vehicle parts under the auto duties, so in Chapter 83 they reach the 58 lines outside Section 232: locks and keys, brass hardware, safes, desk equipment, ornaments and bells, tubing with fittings, buckles and rivets, crown corks, sign plates and welding consumables. USMCA goods are exempt; China's 12.5% stacks with its Lists 3 and 4A.

changes.title: Section 122 surcharge expired
changes.detail: The 10% surcharge on products of all countries (9903.03.01) expired at the close of July 23, 2026. It never applied to Section 232 goods (Proclamation 11012), so in Chapter 83 it had charged only the lines outside Section 232; USMCA goods were exempt.

changes.title: Section 301 tariff on Brazil: Section 232 lines exempt
changes.detail: The 25% duty on goods of Brazil (9903.05.01) took effect. Section 232 goods are excluded (note 50(a)(vi)(1)), so it reaches the 58 non-232 lines of Chapter 83; from July 24 the 12.5% 2026 action (9903.05.27) is added.

changes.title: Proclamation 11032: 85% U.S.-melted test
changes.detail: From June 8, 2026, a derivative article qualifies for the 10% rate (9903.82.06) when at least 85% of its aluminum, steel or copper content by weight was melted, poured, smelted or cast in the United States (Proclamation 11021 had required all of it). Chapter 83 rates (25%) did not change.

changes.title: Taiwan auto-parts rate of 15% (vehicle locks, hinges and fittings)
changes.detail: Under the U.S.-Taiwan agreement, Taiwanese auto parts pay 15% in place of the base rate (9903.94.67), which covers the vehicle locks, hinges and fittings of 8301.20, 8302.10.30 and 8302.30. Similar deal rates apply to the EU (August 1, 2025), Japan (September 16, 2025) and Korea (November 1, 2025); the UK rate is 10% (June 30, 2025).

changes.title: Commerce adds the no-metal heading 9903.82.01
changes.detail: Commerce added heading 9903.82.01 from April 6, 2026: articles on the Section 232 lists that contain no aluminum, steel or copper pay no Section 232 duty. It matters for Chapter 83 fittings of other base metals.

changes.title: Section 232 rebuilt on full value: Chapter 83 derivatives at 25% (Proclamation 11021)
changes.detail: Proclamation 11021 replaced the earlier headings with 9903.82.02–9903.82.26, charged on the full customs value. All 31 Chapter 83 derivative lines moved to the 25% list (9903.82.09), from 50% of the metal content. Articles outside Chapters 72–76 whose listed metal is under 15% of their weight are exempt (9903.82.03); UK goods with 95% UK metal pay 15%, goods of U.S.-melted metal 10%. Manufacturing drawback is allowed for the 25% list from trade-agreement partners; goods admitted to a foreign-trade zone must take privileged foreign status.

changes.title: Section 122 surcharge replaces the IEEPA tariffs; Section 232 goods outside it
changes.detail: A 10% surcharge on products of all countries (9903.03.01) applied until July 23, 2026. Proclamation 11012 says it does not apply in addition to Section 232 duties, so in Chapter 83 only the non-232 lines paid it; USMCA goods were exempt.

changes.title: All IEEPA tariffs end
changes.detail: After the Supreme Court held on February 20, 2026 (Learning Resources, Inc. v. Trump) that IEEPA does not authorize tariffs, Executive Order 14389 ended the Canada, Mexico, China and reciprocal duties, and CBP stopped collecting them from 12:00 a.m. ET on February 24, 2026. Section 232 duties are not IEEPA duties and continued. For Chapter 83 the IEEPA duties had applied to the non-232 lines and to the non-metal content of derivatives.

changes.title: Collated steel staples from China: AD/CVD orders continued
changes.detail: After expedited sunset reviews (dumping margins likely up to 122.55%; subsidy rates up to 63.24%) and the ITC's vote, Commerce continued the antidumping and countervailing duty orders on certain collated steel staples from China (8305.20.0000). Cash deposits continue at the rates in effect at entry.

changes.title: Section 301 tariff on Nicaragua phases in from 2027
changes.detail: Products of Nicaragua that are not CAFTA-DR originating goods will pay +10% from January 1, 2027 and +15% from January 1, 2028 (9903.89.01, U.S. note 29), on every Chapter 83 line. Note 29 has no Section 232 carve-out, so it will add to the 25% on Nicaraguan derivatives. The rate is 0% in 2026.

changes.title: Section 232 on medium- and heavy-duty vehicle parts
changes.detail: Proclamation 10984 imposed 25% on medium- and heavy-duty truck and bus parts (9903.74.08), which reaches the vehicle locks, hinges and fittings of 8301.20, 8302.10.30 and 8302.30 when used as truck parts. USMCA-qualifying parts are exempt (9903.74.10). Korea's 15% auto-parts deal rate took effect the same day.

changes.title: Section 232 inclusions add steel hinges, fittings, staples and caps
changes.detail: Commerce's first inclusions round added steel derivatives 8302.10.60 (hinges), 8302.41.30 (door closers), 8302.41.60, 8302.42.30 and 8302.49.60 (building, furniture and other fittings), 8305.20 (staples in strips) and 8307.10.60 (flexible steel tubing), and aluminum derivatives 8307.90.60.00 and 8309.90.00.20 / .25 (aluminum caps and can ends), at 50% of the metal content.

changes.title: EU auto-parts rate of 15%
changes.detail: EU auto parts, including the vehicle locks, hinges and fittings of 8301.20, 8302.10.30 and 8302.30, pay 15% in place of the base rate (9903.94.53) under the U.S.-EU framework, retroactive to August 1, 2025.

changes.title: Section 232 doubled to 50% on the metal content
changes.detail: Proclamation 10947 raised the aluminum and steel duties from 25% to 50% (UK stayed at 25%). For the Chapter 83 aluminum derivatives it applied to the value of the aluminum content; the non-metal content paid the reciprocal and other IEEPA duties. Ended April 5, 2026.

changes.title: Section 232 on automobile parts (vehicle locks, hinges, fittings)
changes.detail: Proclamation 10908 imposed 25% on automobile parts (9903.94.05), including motor-vehicle locks (8301.20), hinges (8302.10.30) and mountings and fittings (8302.30) when they are passenger-vehicle or light-truck parts. USMCA-qualifying parts were exempt.

changes.title: Reciprocal tariff on Chapter 83 goods
changes.detail: Executive Order 14257 set the reciprocal tariffs from April 5, 2025 (10%, country rates from August 7, 2025). Section 232 goods were excluded (Annex II); for derivatives charged on their metal content, the non-metal content paid it. Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: 24 Chapter 83 lines become Section 232 aluminum derivatives
changes.detail: Proclamation 10895 extended the aluminum duty to the derivative articles listed by Commerce (90 FR 11251) and ended all country exemptions. In Chapter 83 that meant hinges, castors, vehicle, building and furniture fittings, brackets, door closers, binder fittings and frames (8302.10.30–8302.60.90, 8305.10.00.50, 8306.30): 25% on the aluminum content (9903.85.08), and 200% for Russian goods (9903.85.68).

changes.title: IEEPA duties on Canada and Mexico
changes.detail: +25% on goods of Canada (9903.01.10) and Mexico (9903.01.01) from March 4, 2025; USMCA goods exempt from March 7, 2025. Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: Carton-closing staples from China: antidumping order revoked
changes.detail: Commerce revoked the 2018 antidumping order on carton-closing staples from China (8305.20) at its first sunset review because no domestic party took part, effective May 8, 2023.

changes.title: Paper clips from China: antidumping order continued
changes.detail: Commerce and the ITC continued the antidumping order on paper clips wholly of wire of base metal from China (8305.90.3010) after its fifth sunset review; margins likely to prevail up to 126.94%.

changes.title: Aluminum extrusions from China: AD/CVD orders continued
changes.detail: The 2011 antidumping and countervailing duty orders on aluminum extrusions from China were continued. Their HTS list names 23 Chapter 83 lines (aluminum hinges, castors, vehicle, building and furniture fittings, drawer slides, brackets, door-closer parts, binder fittings and frames); finished goods fully assembled at entry and finished goods kits are excluded.

changes.title: Russia: 35% in lieu of column 2 on vehicle fittings and staples
changes.detail: Proclamation 10420 set 35% in place of the column 2 rate (9903.90.08, U.S. note 30(b)) on listed Russian goods, including 8302.30.30 (motor-vehicle fittings) and 8305.20 (staples in strips).

changes.title: China Section 301 List 4A cut to 7.5%
changes.detail: List 4A (9903.88.15), in force since September 1, 2019 at 15%, was cut to 7.5% from February 14, 2020. It covers 24 Chapter 83 lines: most padlocks and locks, lock parts and keys, vehicle hinges, furniture fittings and drawer slides, binder fittings, staples in strips, other office articles and plated ornaments.

changes.title: China Section 301 List 3 raised to 25%
changes.detail: List 3 (9903.88.03) has covered 57 Chapter 83 lines since September 24, 2018 (10%), raised to 25% from May 10, 2019: vehicle locks, hinges, castors, fittings, safes, frames, tubing, buckles, caps, sign plates and welding consumables.

understandIndustry.why:
U.S. imports of Chapter 83 miscellaneous articles of base metal were **$15.10B in 2025**, -6.1% from $16.09B in 2024 (peak: $17.44B in 2022). The five largest suppliers were China ($4.39B), Mexico ($2.89B), Canada ($1.46B), Taiwan ($1.19B), Vietnam ($710M). By product group the largest were hinges, castors & mountings and fittings (8302, $8.55B), padlocks, locks & keys (8301, $2.83B), stoppers, caps, lids & closures (8309, $1.09B). The largest single six-digit line was motor-vehicle mountings and fittings, 8302.30 ($2.60B).

China's shipments fell from $5.62B to $4.39B while Vietnam's rose from $494M to $710M. 2025 was the year Section 232 reached this chapter: 24 hinge, castor, fitting, bracket, door-closer, binder-fitting and frame lines became aluminum derivatives on March 12, and steel hinges and fittings, staples, steel tubing and aluminum caps followed on August 18. Since April 6, 2026 those 31 lines pay 25% of their full value from every country; the rest pay the 2026 Section 301 duties.

2025 is the latest full year of U.S. trade data. Duty-collected figures aren't available from an official source yet.

industryAreas.intro:
Each cell is the base rate for that product group plus the extra duties for that country, minus any preference, from the current tariff schedule. Chapter 83 splits in two. The **31 Section 232 derivative lines** (hinges, castors, door closers and fittings of iron, steel, aluminum or zinc, drawer slides, brackets, staples, frames, flexible tubing without fittings, caps and can ends) pay **25%** plus the base rate from every country, USMCA included, and no 2026 Section 301 duty. The **58 other lines** pay the base rate plus the **2026 Section 301** duty: 10% or 12.5% for most of the 60 economies, 10% or 12.5% *in place of* a lower base rate for the EU, Japan, Korea and Taiwan, and nothing extra for USMCA-qualifying goods of Canada and Mexico.

China pays **25% or 7.5% more** under its Section 301 lists, Canada **+50%** under Section 338 on 18 lines (safes, buckles, crown corks, sign plates, welding consumables) even with USMCA, Brazil 25% + 12.5% on the non-232 lines, and Russia column 2 rates plus 200% on aluminum derivatives. Vehicle locks, hinges and fittings show both answers: the auto or truck parts duty when used as vehicle parts, the metals or Section 301 duty otherwise. The table does **not** include antidumping or countervailing duties (see Tariff updates).

Other lines: 12.5% (9903.05.31) + 25% List 3 or 7.5% List 4A + base: 22%–26% on most locks, 37.5%–45% on safes, buckles, caps, sign plates and welding consumables; 12.5% only on the 8 List 4B lines. industryAreas.exemptionCheck: Read U.S. notes 2, 16, 19, 20, 29, 30, 33, 35, 38, 50, 51 and 52 to Chapter 99 subchapter III in the 2026 Revision 21. Note 16(c)(vi) lists 27 Chapter 83 lines as aluminum derivatives and (vii) 19 as steel derivatives (31 lines in all); the 15% metal-weight test of note 16(c) applies because Chapter 83 is outside Chapters 72–76. No country exemption exists, and note 16(b) collects the duty on top of FTA rates. Section 232 goods are excluded from the 2026 Section 301 duties (note 52(f)(1)), the Brazil duty (note 50(a)(vi)(1)) and the expired Section 122 surcharge, but not from China Section 301 (note 20) or the 2027 Nicaragua duty (note 29). No Chapter 83 line is on the note 52(b) general exemption list or the note 52(j) country exception lists, and no China product exclusion covers Chapter 83 (notes 20(vvv)–(www)). 8310 is on CBP's informational-materials list (9903.05.92, 9903.05.09). Civil aircraft relief (notes 2(v), 35, 51(d), 52(d)) and the 9903.82.01 / 9903.82.03 headings need the importer's confirmation and are not applied.

tariffEngineering.h1: HTS Chapter 83: Miscellaneous Articles of Base Metal — Import Documents & Ways to Lower Duty

seo.title: Importing Locks, Hinges & Hardware: Section 232 Entry, Metal Content, USMCA & Ways to Lower Duty (HTS Ch. 83) | KoalaGains
seo.shortDescription: The rules for each HTS Chapter 83 line: Section 232 headings and the 15% metal-weight test, melt-and-pour and smelt-and-cast reporting, origin marking, USMCA claims, food-contact rules for caps, AD/CVD scope, plus legal ways to pay less: U.S.-melted metal (10%), low metal content, USMCA, informational materials, drawback and correct classification.

tariffEngineering.intro:
For Chapter 83 the paperwork decides which of two regimes applies. On the 31 Section 232 derivative lines the entry reports the Section 232 heading (9903.82.09, or a lower-rate or no-duty heading) next to the Chapter 83 line, the **country where the steel was melted and poured or the aluminum smelted and cast**, and the metal content; the duty is charged on the full value with no FTA reduction. On the other lines the **2026 Section 301** heading for the country of origin is reported, unless a USMCA or informational-materials exemption is claimed. Vehicle locks, hinges and fittings take the auto-parts headings when they are vehicle parts. Every article must be marked with its country of origin, and caps and closures that touch food must meet FDA food-contact rules.

The legal ways to pay less: **metal content under 15% of the weight** (9903.82.03) or of **U.S.-melted metal** (10%), **UK metal** (15%), **USMCA** for Canadian and Mexican goods outside Section 232, **informational-materials** treatment for sign plates, **avoiding Chinese origin**, **drawback**, correct classification (castor size, parts with their parent article) and checking **AD/CVD scope** before buying. Each rule and lever links to its regulation or proclamation.

levers.title: Check the aluminum, steel and copper share of the article's weight
levers.saves: The whole 25% Section 232 duty when the listed metals are under 15% of the weight (9903.82.03) or absent (9903.82.01)
levers.appliesTo: The 31 Section 232 derivative lines of Chapter 83, e.g. fittings with plastic, glass or wood bodies, or of base metals other than aluminum, steel and copper
levers.document: A bill of materials and weights showing the aggregate aluminum, steel and copper content below 15% of the article's weight (or none at all), kept for CBP; enter under 9903.82.03 or 9903.82.01.
levers.caveat: The test is by weight of the listed metals combined. Classification still follows the article: a zinc-alloy hinge stays in 8302.10.60 and pays its base rate. China's Section 301 lists and the 2026 Section 301 duty then apply as for non-232 goods (9903.82.01/.03 are outside the note 52(f)(1) exemption).

citations.label: HTSUS Ch. 99, subch. III, U.S. note 16(c), headings 9903.82.01 and 9903.82.03

levers.title: Use U.S.-melted steel or U.S.-smelted aluminum
levers.saves: 15 points on the Section 232 duty (10% instead of 25%, 9903.82.06)
levers.appliesTo: The 31 Section 232 derivative lines (hinges, castors, fittings, drawer slides, brackets, staples, frames, tubing, caps)
levers.document: Mill and smelter certificates showing that at least 85% (by weight) of the metal content was melted and poured or smelted and cast in the United States; reported in ACE.
levers.caveat: The 85% test applies from June 8, 2026 (before that, all of it). Origin of the article and the base rate do not change; China's Section 301 duty still applies to Chinese-made goods.

citations.label: HTSUS Ch. 99, subch. III, U.S. note 16(e), heading 9903.82.06

levers.title: Buy UK goods made of UK metal
levers.saves: 10 points on the Section 232 duty (15% instead of 25%, 9903.82.05)
levers.appliesTo: The 31 Section 232 derivative lines, for products of the United Kingdom
levers.document: Mill and smelter certificates showing that at least 95% of the steel was melted and poured, or the aluminum smelted and cast, in the UK.
levers.caveat: Origin must be the UK and the 95% test must be met; otherwise 25%.

citations.label: HTSUS Ch. 99, subch. III, U.S. note 16(d)

levers.title: Claim USMCA on Canadian and Mexican goods outside Section 232
levers.saves: The 10% Section 301 duty and the base rate (up to 16.1%) on the 58 non-232 lines; the 25% auto-parts duty on qualifying vehicle locks and fittings
levers.appliesTo: Locks, keys, brass hardware, safes, desk equipment, ornaments, tubing with fittings, buckles, caps, sign plates and welding consumables that originate in Canada or Mexico
levers.document: A USMCA certification of origin from the importer, exporter or producer, available to CBP on request.
levers.caveat: USMCA does not reduce Section 232 (note 16(b)) or the 50% Section 338 duty on 18 Canadian lines (note 51(a)).

citations.label: HTSUS Ch. 99, subch. III, U.S. note 52(g)–(h)

levers.title: Enter qualifying sign plates as informational materials
levers.appliesTo: Sign plates, name plates, numbers, letters and symbols of 8310 that are informational materials
levers.document: Product description showing the plates carry information (signs, notices); enter under 9903.05.92 (and 9903.05.09 for Brazil).
levers.caveat: Does not lift China's 25% List 3 duty or Canada's 50% Section 338 duty. Plain blanks or decorative plates are not informational materials.

levers.title: Avoid Chinese origin
levers.saves: 25% (or 7.5%) of the value: Chinese goods pay Section 301 Lists 3 or 4A on top of Section 232 or the 2026 duty
levers.appliesTo: 81 of the 89 Chapter 83 lines, for goods of China
levers.document: Production records showing where the article was made; origin follows the last substantial transformation (for goods processed in Canada or Mexico, the tariff-shift rules of 19 CFR 102.20). Ask CBP for a binding ruling.
levers.caveat: Section 232 applies to every country, and Chinese parts assembled elsewhere can still fall under AD/CVD orders or circumvention findings.

citations.label: HTSUS Ch. 99, subch. III, U.S. note 20

levers.title: Classify by the chapter notes, not the catalog name
levers.saves: The difference between lines: a castor over 75 mm with a wheel 30 mm or wider is not a Chapter 83 castor (8716.90), parts of base metal go with their parent article, brass fittings are outside Section 232
levers.appliesTo: Castors (8302.20), parts of locks and fittings, hinges and fittings of different metals (8302.10, 8302.41, 8302.42, 8302.49), locks by use (8301.20, .30, .40)
levers.document: Product specifications (wheel diameter and width, metal composition, intended use) and, when in doubt, a CBP binding ruling.
levers.caveat: Screws, bolts, springs and chain of Chapter 73 (7312, 7315, 7317, 7318, 7320) are never parts of Chapter 83 articles (note 1).

levers.title: Drawback on re-exported goods
levers.saves: Up to 99% of the base rate and ordinary duties; Section 232 duty on the 25% list only for goods of trade-agreement partners
levers.appliesTo: Chapter 83 goods used in manufacturing or re-exported; the Section 232 part only for UK, EU, Japan, Korea, Mexico or Canada goods whose metal was melted or smelted in one of them and that are not AD/CVD merchandise
levers.document: A drawback claim to CBP with import and export records (19 CFR part 191).

levers.title: Civil aircraft parts
levers.saves: The base rate (Free (C)) and, for EU, Japan, Korea, UK and Canadian goods on the listed subheadings, the Section 232 or Section 338 duty; the 2026 Section 301 duty for all
levers.appliesTo: Hinges, castors, fittings, door closers and flexible tubing (8302.10.60, 8302.10.90, 8302.20, 8302.42, 8302.49.40–.80, 8302.60.30, 8307.10.30, 8307.90.30) for civil aircraft
levers.document: Certification that the article is for use in civil aircraft under general note 6 and 19 CFR 10.183.
levers.caveat: Military and (except for the UK) unmanned aircraft are excluded.

citations.label: HTSUS Ch. 99, subch. III, U.S. notes 2(v), 35, 51(d), 52(d)

levers.title: Check AD/CVD scope before you buy
levers.saves: The whole antidumping or countervailing duty, when the product or producer is outside the order
levers.appliesTo: Chinese aluminum-extrusion hardware (8302, 8305.10.00.50, 8306.30), paper clips wholly of wire (8305.90.30.10) and collated steel staples (8305.20)
levers.document: The order's written scope (it, not the HTS number, decides) and the producer's company-specific cash-deposit rate; when unsure, request a scope ruling from Commerce.
levers.caveat: A product in scope pays the cash deposit even if entered under another HTS line. Finished goods fully assembled at entry (e.g. framed pictures with glass) and finished goods kits are outside the extrusions orders.

seo.shortDescription: Answers to what people search about U.S. tariffs on HTS Chapter 83: HS codes 8301 and 8302 for locks and hinges, drawer slides, the aluminum and steel derivative list, China, Mexico and Canada (Section 338), the 2026 Section 301 duties, caps, sign plates, frames, staples and welding wire.

finalConclusion.intro: Straight answers to the most-searched questions about U.S. tariffs on miscellaneous articles of base metal (HTS Chapter 83), by product, by country and by HS code. Each answer links to the page with the detail and the official sources.
keyTakeaways: 31 of the 89 Chapter 83 lines are Section 232 aluminum or steel derivatives (hinges, castors, door closers and fittings of iron, steel, aluminum or zinc, drawer slides, brackets, staples, frames, tubing without fittings, caps and can ends): 25% of the full value from every country since April 6, 2026, on top of any FTA or USMCA rate.

The other 58 lines (locks and keys, brass hardware, safes, ornaments, buckles, crown corks, sign plates, welding consumables) pay the 2026 Section 301 duty of 10% or 12.5% since July 24, 2026; USMCA goods of Canada and Mexico are exempt. Vehicle locks, hinges and fittings pay the auto-parts duty when used in vehicles.

China pays 25% (List 3) or 7.5% (List 4A) more on 81 lines, Canada +50% Section 338 on 18 lines even with USMCA, and Chinese aluminum-extrusion hardware, paper clips and collated staples carry AD/CVD. The IEEPA tariffs ended February 24, 2026 and the Section 122 surcharge July 23, 2026.
In 2025 the U.S. imported $15.10B of Chapter 83 products; China ($4.39B) and Mexico ($2.89B) were the largest suppliers.

faqs.question: What is HTS Chapter 83?
faqs.answer: Chapter 83 of the Harmonized Tariff Schedule covers miscellaneous articles of base metal: padlocks, locks and keys (8301), hinges, castors and mountings and fittings for doors, windows, furniture and vehicles (8302), safes (8303), desk equipment (8304), binder fittings, paper clips and staples (8305), bells, ornaments, frames and mirrors (8306), flexible tubing (8307), clasps, buckles, eyelets and rivets (8308), caps, crown corks and can ends (8309), sign plates (8310) and welding electrodes and solder (8311). It has 89 ten-digit lines. In 2025 the U.S. imported $15.10B of them, led by China and Mexico.

faqs.question: What is the HS code and tariff for hinges (HS 8302)?
faqs.answer: Heading 8302 covers base-metal mountings and fittings; hinges are 8302.10: 8302.10.30 for motor-vehicle hinges of iron, steel, aluminum or zinc (2%), 8302.10.60 for other hinges of those metals (3.5%; door, furniture and other), and 8302.10.90 for hinges of other base metal such as brass (3.4%). Iron, steel, aluminum or zinc hinges are Section 232 derivatives: +25% of the value from every country (a Vietnamese steel door hinge pays 28.5%, a Chinese one 53.5%). Brass hinges are not; they pay the 2026 Section 301 duty instead.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for drawer slides and cabinet hardware?
faqs.answer: Drawer slides of iron, steel, aluminum or zinc are 8302.42.30.15 (furniture fittings, 3.9%); gas lift cylinders for furniture are 8302.42.30.10, other furniture fittings 8302.42.30.65, and fittings of other base metal 8302.42.60 (3.4%). Door and window hardware for buildings is 8302.41. The 8302.42.30 and 8302.41.30/.60 lines pay 25% Section 232 from every country; Chinese drawer slides add 7.5% (List 4A) for 36.4%, and aluminum ones can fall under the aluminum extrusions AD/CVD orders.

faqs.question: What is the tariff code for locks and padlocks (HS 8301)?
faqs.answer: Heading 8301: padlocks 8301.10 (2.3% to 6.1% by width and construction), motor-vehicle locks 8301.20 (5.7%), furniture locks 8301.30 (5.7%), door locks, locksets and other locks 8301.40 (luggage locks 3.1%, others 5.7%), clasps with locks 8301.50, parts 8301.60 and keys 8301.70. Locks are not on the Section 232 metals lists: most countries add 10% or 12.5% Section 301 (none for USMCA goods), China adds 12.5% plus 7.5% (List 4A) on most lines. Car and truck locks pay the auto-parts duty instead.

faqs.question: Which Chapter 83 products are on the Section 232 aluminum and steel derivative list?
searchedAs: steel and aluminum tariffs derivative products
faqs.answer: U.S. note 16(c) to Chapter 99 lists 31 Chapter 83 lines: hinges of iron, steel, aluminum or zinc (8302.10.30, 8302.10.60), castors (8302.20), vehicle fittings (8302.30.30), door closers (8302.41.30, 8302.60), building, furniture and other fittings including drawer slides (8302.41.60, 8302.42.30, 8302.49.60), brackets (8302.50), binder fittings (8305.10.00.50), staples in strips (8305.20), frames and mirrors (8306.30), flexible tubing without fittings (8307.10.60, 8307.90.60) and aluminum or steel caps and can ends (8309.90.00.20, .25, .80). Since April 6, 2026 all pay 25% of the full value (9903.82.09), or none if aluminum, steel and copper are under 15% of the weight.

faqs.question: What are the tariffs on Chapter 83 goods from China in 2026?
searchedAs: what are the tariffs on china
faqs.answer: On the 31 Section 232 lines China pays 25% Section 232 plus 25% (List 3) or 7.5% (List 4A) plus the base rate: about 50%–55.7% on hinges, castors and fittings, 36.4% on drawer slides. On the other lines it pays 12.5% (2026 Section 301) plus 25% or 7.5%: most locks 22%–26%, safes 41.3%, buckles, crown corks, sign plates and welding electrodes 37.5% or more. Chinese aluminum-extrusion hardware, paper clips and collated staples also carry AD/CVD. The IEEPA tariffs on China ended February 24, 2026. China shipped $4.39B of Chapter 83 goods in 2025.

faqs.question: What is the tariff on Chapter 83 goods from Mexico?
faqs.answer: Mexican goods outside Section 232 (locks, safes, buckles, crown corks, sign plates, welding consumables) are Free with a USMCA certification of origin; without it they pay the base rate plus 10% Section 301 (9903.05.55). The 31 Section 232 lines (hinges, fittings, drawer slides, brackets, caps) pay 25% with or without USMCA. USMCA-qualifying vehicle locks and fittings pay no auto-parts duty. Mexico shipped $2.89B of Chapter 83 goods in 2025.

faqs.question: Which Chapter 83 goods are on the Section 338 list for Canada?
faqs.answer: Section 338 of the Tariff Act of 1930 lets the President add duties on countries that discriminate against U.S. commerce. Under Proclamations 11048 and 11065, 18 Chapter 83 lines from Canada pay +50% (9903.03.14) even with a USMCA claim: lock parts, safes and other ornaments since August 22, 2026, and flexible tubing with fittings, all of 8308 (buckles, eyelets, rivets, clasps), crown corks, sign plates and welding electrodes, cored wire and solders since September 15, 2026 (CBP CSMS 69851916). Other Canadian lines pay 25% Section 232 or nothing extra with USMCA. Canada shipped $1.46B of Chapter 83 goods in 2025.

faqs.question: Are the Section 301 tariffs of July 24, 2026 and the Section 122 surcharge still in effect?
searchedAs: are the tariffs still in effect
faqs.answer: The 2026 Section 301 duties on 60 economies (10% or 12.5%) took effect July 24, 2026 and apply to the 58 Chapter 83 lines outside Section 232; USMCA goods are exempt. The 10% Section 122 surcharge expired July 23, 2026, and the IEEPA tariffs ended February 24, 2026 after the Supreme Court ruling. Section 232 and the China Section 301 lists continue.

faqs.question: What is HS code 8309 (caps, crown corks and lids)?
faqs.answer: Heading 8309 covers stoppers, caps and lids of base metal: crown corks 8309.10 (Free) and other caps, can ends, screw caps and seals 8309.90 (2.6%), split into aluminum beverage-can ends (.20), other aluminum (.25), steel (.80) and other (.85). The aluminum and steel lines are Section 232 derivatives at 25%; crown corks pay the 2026 Section 301 duty (Canada +50% Section 338). Closures that touch food must meet FDA food-contact rules (21 CFR 177.1210).

faqs.question: What is the tariff code for welding wire and welding rods?
faqs.answer: Coated stick electrodes for arc welding are 8311.10, flux-cored wire 8311.20, coated rods and cored wire for soldering, brazing or flame welding 8311.30 (lead-tin solders 8311.30.30) and other 8311.90; all are Free and not on the Section 232 lists, so they pay the 2026 Section 301 duty (10%–12.5%), China 12.5% + 25%, Canada +50% Section 338. Solid (uncoated) MIG wire is classified with its metal, e.g. steel welding wire in Chapter 72, where Section 232 applies.

faqs.question: What is HS code 8310 (metal signs and name plates)?
faqs.answer: 8310.00.00.00 covers sign plates, name plates, address plates, numbers, letters and other symbols of base metal (illuminated signs are 9405). It is Free and not on the Section 232 lists. Heading 8310 is on CBP's informational-materials list, so plates that qualify enter under 9903.05.92 without the 2026 Section 301 duty; others pay 10% or 12.5%. China adds 25% (List 3) and Canada 50% (Section 338).

faqs.question: What is the HS code for metal picture frames and ornaments (HS 8306)?
faqs.answer: Heading 8306: non-electric bells and gongs 8306.10 (5.8%), ornaments plated with precious metal 8306.21 (4.5%), other statuettes and ornaments 8306.29 (Free), and photograph or picture frames and mirrors of base metal 8306.30 (2.7%). Frames and mirrors are a Section 232 aluminum derivative (25%); ornaments and bells pay the 2026 Section 301 duty. Chinese aluminum frames can fall under the extrusions AD/CVD orders unless entered as finished framed pictures with glass and backing.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for staples and paper clips, and do they carry antidumping duties?
faqs.answer: Staples in strips are 8305.20 (Free) and paper clips 8305.90.30 (Free; wholly of wire .10); ring-binder mechanisms are 8305.10.00.10. Staples in strips pay 25% Section 232 from every country. Chinese collated steel staples are under antidumping and countervailing duty orders continued in February 2026, and Chinese paper clips wholly of wire under an antidumping order continued in 2023.
